    <item>
      <title>Hilarious quips and ‘100,000-volt’ energy: the hypemen (and women) redefining Afrobeats music</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/lagos-hypemen-redefining-afrobeats-music-afrohype</link>
      <description><p>Style of emceeing based on high-octane, ad-libbed vocals has flourished thanks to its unique way of captivating crowds</p><p>For the 2015 freshmen cohort of the history degree programme at the University of Lagos, their classmate’s first-semester presentation was so captivating that they began calling him Toby Shang, after the 16th-century Chinese dynasty he had focused on.</p><p>His crowd engagement that day had been harnessed from his high school days as a ginger-man (energiser) in a three-man band and as a private tutor. By his final year at university, his viral catchphrases and infectious energy had resulted in a hit song, Shedibalabala. Today, he is one of the self-acclaimed “evangelists and pioneers” in the Afrobeats sub-genre some are now calling Afrohype or lamba.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/lagos-hypemen-redefining-afrobeats-music-afrohype">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>A girl called Àìná was captured by an African king and later taken to England to become Sarah Forbes Bonetta, protege of the imperial monarch </p><p>When she was seven years old, Bayo Randle’s great-great-grandmother Sarah Forbes Bonetta was presented to Queen Victoria at Windsor Castle as a “diplomatic gift” from an African king.</p><p>Victoria would go on to pay for Bonetta’s education, approve her marriage to one of west Africa’s wealthiest men, and become godmother to her eldest daughter.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/18/sarah-forbes-bonetta-biography-queen-victoria">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>LGBTQ+ people go into hiding in Senegal as hundreds are arrested</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch</link>
      <description><p>At least 320 people detained for ‘acts against nature’ after law criminalising homosexuality toughened, HRW reports</p><p>Mass arrests, forced HIV testing and barriers to legal representation are part of an escalating crackdown against LGBTQ+ people in Senegal, according to a <a href="https://www.hrw.org/news/2026/10/12/senegal-brutal-crackdown-violates-lgbt-peoples-rights">new report</a>.</p><p>More than 320 individuals have been arrested and detained on allegations of “acts against nature” since February, <a href="https://www.hivjustice.net/cases/senegal-crackdown-on-lgbtq-people-intensifies-with-multiple-arrests/">according to HIV Justice Network</a>, an organisation quoted in the Human Rights Watch (HRW) report. Among these, at least 84 were charged with “voluntary HIV transmission”, solely on the basis of their HIV status.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/global-development/2026/oct/15/senegal-homosexuality-criminalised-anti-lgbtq-arrests-hiv-testing-human-rights-watch">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/oct/14/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-denies-ai-story</link>
      <description><p>Article in Atlantic claims The Blue Fighter was artificially generated, days after it won Caine prize for African writers</p><p>The Zimbabwean writer Simbarashe Kundizeza has denied using AI to write a prize-winning short story after an article in the Atlantic said software had flagged it as almost completely AI-generated.</p><p>Kundizeza’s story <a href="https://static1.squarespace.com/static/6a4f3fb6a6178e0225b39a4c/t/6a95fffc36f1fc568e02f7fe/1788215293124/3.The+Blue+Fighter.pdf">The Blue Fighter</a> was announced as the winner of the prestigious Caine prize for African writers on 6 October. Five days later, The Atlantic published an <a href="https://www.theatlantic.com/books/2026/10/caine-prize-winning-short-story-seems-be-ai/688967/">article</a> by the author and journalist Vauhini Vara titled: “Yet Another Literary prize winner Seems to Be AI.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/oct/14/zimbabwean-author-simbarashe-kundizeza-denies-ai-story">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Guinea-Bissau denies it has approved controversial vaccine trial in newborns</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial</link>
      <description><p>Health minister says government ‘did not authorize’ Danish-led hepatitis B trial in babies backed by RFK Jr</p><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/guinea-bissau">Guinea-Bissau</a> has not approved the controversial <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/hepatitis-b">hepatitis B</a> study in newborns that would be funded by the US government and private partners, the African country’s minister of health said on Tuesday.</p><p>The study, which would not investigate the safety or effectiveness of vaccines but would instead track “nonspecific” health outcomes like overall mortality or neurodevelopmental conditions, has been championed by Robert F Kennedy Jr, secretary of the US Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and a longtime anti-vaccine activist.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/oct/14/guinea-bissau-vaccine-hepatitis-b-trial-denial">Continue reading...</a></description>

News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/</link><lastBuildDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 11:55:25 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category></category><title>Paris protests: A look at the aftermath</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261018-paris-protests-a-look-at-the-aftermath</link><description>
Following yesterday's demonstrations in Paris, where violent clashes erupted between police and protesters, our reporter Antonia Kerrigan returns to place de la République.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2184975a-cae6-11f1-8154-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261018-130127-131615-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2184975a-cae6-11f1-8154-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261018-130127-131615-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">265d43d0-cae6-11f1-a4a9-b7e4c9b2dcc0</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 11:51:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Americas</category><title>Atlanta’s iconic tavern marks Georgia’s past with an eye on future as midterms approach</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/americas/20261018-atlanta-iconic-tavern-marks-georgia-past-eye-future-midterms-approach-ossoff-collins</link><description>
Since it was established in 1956, Manuel’s Tavern in Atlanta has hosted legendary Democratic leaders while its founder played a key role in the city’s move from a Republican to Democratic stronghold. With the state’s Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff leading the polls in the midterms amid rumours of a future presidential run, the tavern is once more at the heart of the political action.   
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fa2b4854-c967-11f1-a45e-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/manuels-main.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fa2b4854-c967-11f1-a45e-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/manuels-main.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">08f298ba-c968-11f1-84d4-7b0775633891</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 11:15:04 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/fa2b4854-c967-11f1-a45e-6313a763b466/w:1024/p:16x9/manuels-main.jpg">© Branden Camp, AP</source><dc:creator>Leela JACINTO</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Out-of-control truck kills 13 at Hindu festival in India</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261018-out-of-control-truck-kills-13-at-hindu-festival-in-india</link><description>
A speeding truck in India killed 13 people when it ploughed into a crowd at a Hindu festival, officials said on Sunday, with President Droupadi Murmu describing the deaths as "heartbreaking".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/eab05edc-cae3-11f1-bd72-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261018-121827-121952-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/eab05edc-cae3-11f1-bd72-d1d2c32ebb87/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261018-121827-121952-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ef82c0a8-cae3-11f1-bb9a-01e0b5eaecde</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 11:14:44 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>Riots in Tirana enter a fifth day as Albania's anti-government protests escalate</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261018-riots-in-tirana-enter-a-fifth-day-as-albania-s-anti-government-protests-escalate</link><description>
Clashes broke out near the Albanian prime minister’s office in the capital, Tirana, on Saturday as anti-government riots entered a fifth day.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/62af44a8-cae3-11f1-9366-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261018-111149-111349-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/62af44a8-cae3-11f1-9366-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261018-111149-111349-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">678afb98-cae3-11f1-86ab-cb0ddd5ab1e1</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 11:06:39 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item><item><category></category><title>France: Protests "brought the entire population together for a common purpose"</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/video/20261018-france-protests-brought-the-entire-population-together-for-a-common-purpose</link><description>
This weekend, in cities across France, some 800,000 protesters, including students, railway workers and members of the Yellow Vest movement, took to the streets in largely peaceful nationwide demonstrations. Sparked by a month of high school student protests over educational inequality and crumbling school facilities, the movement has grown into a broader outcry over the cost of living, public spending and climate inaction, as people across France say they have reached their breaking point.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5b3222c4-cad2-11f1-9b89-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261018-101748-102037-CS.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/5b3222c4-cad2-11f1-9b89-4dd8ac2cf3bf/w:1024/p:16x9/EN-20261018-101748-102037-CS.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5fffff24-cad2-11f1-a1a3-2f27257a22bd</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:05:03 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>FRANCE24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

<![CDATA[ Latest from Space.com ]]> https://www.space.com/feeds.xml Sun, 18 Oct 2026 12:00:00 +0000 en <![CDATA[ Astronomers want your help finding 'missing' black holes in the Milky Way ]]> Astronomers estimate that our home galaxy, the Milky Way, has churned out more than 10 million black holes over its 13-billion-year history. Yet so far, they have found only 70.

Now, a group of astronomers in the U.K. is trying to close that vast gap by enlisting the public. Their project, called Black Hole Hunters, is looking for volunteers with a computer and a few spare minutes to sift through troves of data gathered by a NASA space telescope. By flagging recognizable patterns that could point to a "missing" black hole, volunteers can help fast-track a search that would otherwise take years, the team says.

"You'll be narrowing down precisely where we need to point our telescopes next," project co-lead Adam McMaster, an astronomer at the University of Southampton in the U.K., said in a statement, "and you might be the one to discover a black hole."

Cosmic magnifying glasses

Black holes form when massive stars roughly 20 times heavier than our sun run out of fuel and collapse, leaving behind an abyss with gravity so immense that even light cannot escape. While invisible themselves, these cosmic behemoths reveal their presence by bending the light of nearby objects, and the Black Hole Hunters project is searching for one specific manifestation of this effect.

It happens thanks to the fact that massive stars often form in pairs, and a star can sometimes survive the violent supernova explosion that turns its companion into a black hole. When that happens, the two bodies continue to orbit each other. If such a duo aligns just right with Earth, the black hole will periodically pass directly between its companion star and our planet. And when it does, the black hole's gravity acts like a cosmic magnifying glass, bending and magnifying the star's light, causing it to briefly appear brighter to watchful telescopes.

To find these hidden giants, the project relies on data from NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite, or TESS. Although the satellite's primary mission is to hunt for planets beyond our solar system, its method of data collection — tracking tiny, continuous changes in a star's brightness over time — is ideally suited for identifying black hole magnification events, the project description notes.

"It's a simple task with no expertise required," McMaster said in the statement. "We will show volunteers examples of what to look for so all they have to do is recognise the right patterns."

Automated algorithms conduct a preliminary sweep of the TESS data, screening millions of potential stars for the most obvious black hole candidate locations, according to the project description. But, the researchers say, artificial intelligence struggles with the messy realities of the cosmos, such as stellar flares and the natural pulsations of stars that can trick the algorithms into false positives.

The human touch

That makes human volunteers a key part of the search. To keep errors in check, each graph is shown to multiple volunteers, and their answers are combined so that individual mistakes average out, according to the project's website.

"I can search for black holes on my laptop from my bedroom — and could make a real impact on real space science," Grace Clarke, an undergraduate student of physics and astronomy at the University of Southampton who's involved with the project, said in the same statement. "The data's easy to understand — it's just pattern recognition — and you don't need a degree in astronomy to read it."

The crowdsourced shortlist of promising signals lets astronomers aim follow-up observations at specific stars, such as precise measurements of whether a star is being tugged at by an unseen companion. Those measurements take time and are expensive, so a good shortlist helps researchers spend scarce telescope time wisely, the team says.

Since launching on the Zooniverse platform in October 2021, the project has attracted nearly 23,000 volunteers, who have completed more than 12 million classifications, according to its website.

Before turning to TESS, the team ran a similar search using data from SuperWASP, a ground-based survey that, like TESS, monitored stars for signs of planets from 2004 to 2016. Those results are still being analyzed and are expected to be published soon.

The team also plans to widen its search with observations from other instruments, including the European Space Agency's Euclid mission and NASA's recently launched Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope.

"With potentially thousands of new discoveries, we need all the help we can get," McMaster said in the statement.

]]> <![CDATA[ 10 best places to see the 2027 total solar eclipse in Spain ]]> Spain is one of the easiest places in the world to experience the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027. The so-called "eclipse of the century" first makes landfall in Andalucía, where totality will last up to 4 minutes and 40 seconds during mid-morning, with the sun comfortably high at around 38-42 degrees above the horizon in the eastern sky. Excellent roads, plentiful accommodation and Málaga's international airport make this an obvious alternative to North Africa and the Middle East.

However, choosing where to watch requires some thought. Southern Spain's narrowing shape funnels the path toward the Strait of Gibraltar, potentially concentrating huge numbers of eclipse chasers around Tarifa, the Costa del Sol and the British Overseas Territory of Gibraltar during the peak summer holiday season.

From busy Mediterranean beaches to mountain villages, here's where to see the total solar eclipse on Aug. 2, 2027 in southern Spain. All times, totality durations and historical cloud cover data come from Time and Date.

1. Tarifa

Location: Cádiz province

Start of totality and duration: 10:45 a.m. CEST; 4 minutes, 40 seconds

Historical August cloud cover: 13%

Altitude of the sun: 38 degrees above east

At the southernmost tip of mainland Europe, where the Atlantic Ocean meets the Mediterranean Sea, Tarifa is likely to be one of the country's busiest eclipse-watching locations because it will experience the longest totality in mainland Spain. Just 9 miles (14 km) across the Strait of Gibraltar from Morocco, the historic port town is known for its whitewashed old town, the medieval Castle of Guzmán el Bueno and its long, sandy beaches. Los Lances and Valdevaqueros offer wide horizons and plenty of open space.

2. Gaucín

Location: Málaga province, Andalucía, Spain

Start of totality and duration: 10:46 a.m. CEST; 3 minutes, 13 seconds

Historical August cloud cover: 5%

Altitude of the sun: 38 degrees above east

For eclipse chasers who would rather head into the mountains than join the crowds on the Costa del Sol, Gaucín is an intriguing alternative. One of Andalucía's classic pueblos blancos, the whitewashed village occupies a spectacular position in the mountains above the coast, crowned by the ruins of Castillo del Águila. Its elevated setting offers sweeping views across the surrounding countryside towards Gibraltar and, on clear days, the mountains of North Africa. Crucially, heading inland doesn't sacrifice too much totality.

3. Gibraltar

Location: Gibraltar

Start of totality and duration: 10:45 a.m. CEST; 4 minutes, 29 seconds

Historical August cloud cover: 17%

Altitude of the sun: 38 degrees above east

Few places in Europe could provide a more dramatic setting for totality than Gibraltar, the tiny British Overseas Territory dominated by its famous 1,398-foot (426-meter) limestone Rock. However, eclipse chasers will need to view either from The Rock or its east coast, where elevated viewpoints and beaches face the Mediterranean and the eclipsed sun. However, Gibraltar has a potential complication — the easterly Levanter wind can create a distinctive cap of cloud over the Rock even when surrounding skies are clear. Another issue is accommodation, which is already at a premium. See Gibraltar Eclipse 2027.

4. La Línea de la Concepción

Location: Cádiz province

Start of totality and duration: 10:45 a.m. CEST; 4 minutes, 24 seconds

Historical August cloud cover: 17%

Altitude of the sun: 38 degrees above east

Immediately north of Gibraltar, La Línea de la Concepción occupies the sandy isthmus between the Bay of Gibraltar and the Mediterranean Sea. Its location creates one of Spain's most distinctive possibilities for eclipse photography. On the Mediterranean side, Playa de Santa Bárbara is a wide sandy beach north of the border, with the immense Rock of Gibraltar rising to the south — a potentially spectacular foreground. The city has around 9 miles (14 kilometers) of coastline, providing plenty of alternatives for eclipse viewing.

5. Estepona

Location: Costa del Sol, Málaga province

Start of totality and duration: 10:46 a.m. CEST; 3 minutes, 41 seconds

Historical August cloud cover: 7%

Altitude of the sun: 38 degrees above east

About an hour's drive southwest of Málaga Airport, Estepona is one of the Costa del Sol's most attractive resort towns, with a pedestrianized old quarter of whitewashed streets, colorful flowerpots and squares centered on Plaza de las Flores. For eclipse day, the mile-long Playa de la Rada is the obvious gathering place, with its broad Mediterranean horizon and proximity to the town center. Other attractions include Estepona Marina and the Sierra Bermeja mountains rising behind the coast.

6. Cádiz

Location: Cádiz province

Start of totality and duration: 10:45 a.m. CEST; 2 minutes, 56 seconds

Historical August cloud cover: 13%

Altitude of the sun: 37 degrees above east

Historic Cádiz occupies a narrow peninsula jutting into the Atlantic and is packed with reminders of its long maritime past, including the Cádiz Cathedral, the Roman Theatre and Torre Tavira, one of more than 100 watchtowers once used to spot approaching ships. For eclipse day, the long, sandy Playa de la Victoria offers plenty of open space, while La Caleta provides a more historic setting between two coastal castles.

7. Málaga

Location: Málaga province

Start of totality and duration: 10:48 a.m. CEST; 2 minutes

Historical August cloud cover: 9%

Altitude of the sun: 39 degrees above east

Málaga may lose some duration compared with locations farther west, but it makes up for it with excellent transport links, plentiful accommodation and all the attractions of a major Mediterranean city. It combines the hilltop Gibralfaro Castle and Moorish Alcazaba with a Roman theatre, cathedral, museums and a lively historic center. For eclipse day, the obvious option is the coast. La Malagueta beach is within walking distance of the city center, while numerous beaches extend east and west along the Costa del Sol.

8. Torremolinos

Location: Málaga province

Start of totality and duration: 10:47 a.m. CEST; 2 minutes, 46 seconds

Historical August cloud cover: 11%

Altitude of the sun: 39 degrees above east

One of the best-known resorts on Spain's Costa del Sol, Torremolinos combines a long Mediterranean beachfront with easy access to Málaga and its international airport. Its 4-mile (6-kilometer) promenade links broad sandy beaches, including Playa del Bajondillo and Playa de la Carihuela, offering plenty of potential eclipse-watching spots with views toward the eastern sky. For a higher vantage point, nearby Mount Calamorro rises almost 2,600 feet (800 meters) above Benalmádena, with panoramic views across the Costa del Sol and, on clear days, towards Gibraltar and North Africa.

9. Marbella

Location: Costa del Sol, Málaga province

Start of totality and duration: 10:46 a.m. CEST; 3 minutes, 21 seconds

]]> <![CDATA[ 'Let's all choose to make tomorrow better', Artemis II astronauts honored with Stephen Hawking Medal at Starmus ]]> TENERIFE, CANARY ISLANDS — The Artemis II astronauts may have traveled hundreds of thousands of miles away from Earth to the moon, but they made sure the rest of us didn't miss out on the adventure.

Now, their efforts to bring the wonders of space exploration back down to Earth have earned them one of science communication's most prestigious honors: the Stephen Hawking Medal.

NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman and Victor Glover, alongside Canadian Space Agency astronaut Jeremy Hansen, accepted the award on Saturday (Oct. 17), during the opening ceremony of the Starmus VIII festival. The honor recognizes all four crew members, including NASA astronaut Christina Koch, who wasn't in attendance.

For Wiseman, the experience of seeing our home planet from the vicinity of the moon carried a powerful message.

"If we could take each of you 250,000 miles away from this planet, 400,000 kilometers away from planet Earth, and you would see Earth the size of your thumb. It's tiny," Wiseman told the audience.

"When you're there looking through the moon, back at this tiny Earth, the only thing you feel is love, peace, hope, unity", he continued. "Those aren't the right words, but that is all you feel."

During their historic Artemis II mission, the astronauts did far more than put NASA's Orion spacecraft through its paces. Through live communications, interviews and glimpses into life aboard the spacecraft, not to mention the jaw-dropping photos that just keep on coming, they helped turn an extraordinarily complex mission into something people worldwide could experience and connect with.

And that's exactly what the Stephen Hawking Medal is designed to celebrate.

Established in 2016 by physicist Stephen Hawking and Starmus, the award honors those who have gone above and beyond to make science accessible, engaging and inspiring.

The Artemis II crew joins some pretty impressive company. Previous recipients include Apollo 11 moonwalker Buzz Aldrin, naturalist David Attenborough, primatologist Jane Goodall and astrophysicist Neil DeGrasse Tyson.

This year's ceremony marks the medal's 10th anniversary, with filmmaker Ridley Scott also among the 2026 honourees.

"It's a special thrill for us at Starmus to be able to honor the intrepid Artemis II crew members in the same way that we honored the Apollo astronauts who paved the way to the moon over 50 years ago," Starmus co-founder and Queen guitarist Brian May said in a statement ahead of the ceremony.

Wiseman left the audience with one final thought.

"When you come home to this beautiful planet, you realise that it's in every single one of us to choose to make tomorrow better," he said. "So let's all choose to make tomorrow better".

Starmus VIII runs from Oct. 17-22 across Tenerife and La Palma in the Canary Islands. This year's festival, themed "The Search for Truth", brings together leading scientists, astronauts, musicians and artists to celebrate scientific discovery and explore the importance of evidence and scientific thinking.

]]> <![CDATA[ On this day in space! Oct. 17, 2016: Private Antares rocket returns to flight after catastrophic launch explosion ]]>

On Oct. 17, 2016, Orbital ATK (now Northrop Grumman Space Systems) returned to flight, successfully launching a cargo shipment to the International Space Station (ISS) after its previous cargo mission failed to launch.

The private spaceflight company was contracted by NASA to fly cargo to the ISS, and stakes were high for this launch. Orbital ATK's last attempt nearly two years earlier ended in a catastrophic explosion a few seconds after liftoff.

Despite some delays, the newly upgraded Antares rocket flawlessly blasted off into the night sky from NASA's Wallops Flight Facility in Virginia. Six days later, the Cygnus cargo spacecraft arrived at the ISS to deliver food, supplies and science experiments to the crew.

Why it mattered

For the International Space Station to be able to sustain a continuous human occupancy, periodic cargo deliveries are needed. Russia fulfills part of this requirement with its Progress spacecraft, and both ESA (European Space Agency) and JAXA (Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency) have contributed with their Automated Transfer Vehicle (ATV) and H-II Transfer Vehicle (HTV), respectively.

For its part, NASA contracted with Orbital (today, Northrop Grumman) and SpaceX to fly commercial resupply service missions. Both were needed to keep the U.S. operating segment of the station well supplied and with the science and research materials needed for the crew's work.

Below is a video of the explosion

Though adjustments can be made to go without one or more of these vehicles for a short period of time, the Progress, Cygnus and Dragon are key components of the ISS's continuous operation. So returning a vehicle to flight after a catastrophic exploration is important to well-being of the International Space Station program.

As it happened, Antares would fly another 12 times before having to stand down again to be redesigned, but that is for a different This Day in Space entry.

Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'Lanterns' shocking finale left us with a lot of unanswered questions for a potential season 2 ]]> HBO and HBO Max's "Lanterns" served up its big cliffhanger finale on Oct. 4, 2026, and we’ve been slowly digesting thoughts on what the creative direction and ultimate legacy of this debut season were.

While by no means a perfect experiment in trying to shake up the aging superhero genre, there are enough worthy elements to consider this sci-fi mystery show an evolutionary step towards the next generation of comic-based storytelling.

After the emerald-tinted dust has settled, there are many lingering questions about where this acclaimed series from creators Chris Mundy, Damon Lindelof, and Tom King might be headed and where the twists and turns might lead for a sophomore season should it be greenlit (get it?) for a triumphant return.

Warning: Major Spoilers For "Lanterns" Season 1 Ahead!

One of "Lanterns"' standout achievements is revealing the true costs of superheroism by deconstructing its DNA and examining the ugly guts of it all.

It dives into the fear, trauma, and seduction that drive humans to take up the serious business of protecting the universe and doling out justice against both Earth-bound evil and intergalactic threats. "Lanterns" also explores mental health issues and PTSD that are the inevitable byproducts of a life of unimaginable violence. The compelling series achieves a provocative dissection of it all with rare confidence without the overindulgence of distracting CGI tossed in for sheer spectacle.

It might not have been exactly the Green Lantern TV series fans wanted, but it was the show we got, and kinda the show we needed. Sure, for a series about a noble order of intergalactic space cops, we were treated to very little cosmic action, and instead we're given a grounded slow-burn police procedural à la "True Detective."

As I said before, it's not perfect, but we shouldn’t dismiss "Lanterns" for its mild shortcomings when it gets so much right. We're willing a second season into existence, and with an average of 20 million global viewers and solid reviews, HBO/HBO Max would be very wise to bring it back.

Whether a second season shifts into the heavens to rocket off on an outer space trajectory for a follow-up season is yet to be seen. For now, though, the Lanterns season one finale has left us with plenty of questions to ponder.

Is Hal Jordan really dead?

"Lanterns"' season finale revealed that Kerry, in an unhinged moment of maternal panic trying to protect her mutant son, Noah, had put a bullet in Hal's head. RIP to the original Green Lantern... or is it?

Kyle Chandler was a fantastic choice to play Hal Jordan, and he brought a charismatic gravitas and twisted sense of humor to the storied comic character. His sudden death in Rushville, frozen in the bleachers of the high school football stadium, certainly looked final, but this is the wild topsy-turvy universe of superheroes, so anything is possible.

And don’t forget that the newly-freed Thaal Sinestro (Ulrich Thomsen) told the AI “Halogram” and Aaron Pierre’s John Stewart on Antaan's dead planet that the magical green ring could be used to restore Hal’s life. But Sinestro is a sly, slippery foe and is never to be trusted!

Online speculation has proposed that Hal Jordan might be revived and enter the series as Parallax, the living embodiment of fear, but that’s not likely according to the series creators. What’s more probable is that we either see Chandler's Hal Jordan revived, or he'll just turn up in occasional flashbacks or Halogram pop-in scenes.

John Stewart goes rogue?

With his unsanctioned lantern battery now in hand to power his ring, Stewart has become an independent contractor protecting Earth for Guy Gardner’s (Nathan Fillion) Sector 2814.

Fortified with the Sinestro-forged yellow charging unit deemed illegal by the Guardians and the broader members of the Green Lantern Corps., this unattached Lantern is now free to make sure Noah doesn’t turn to the dark side and lean into his evil Manhunter programming.

Will Stewart be seduced into the path of corruption by using Sinestro’s emotionally tainted battery, or steel himself against ill influences and continue to blaze his own trail as Earth's sole protector for the time being?

As a gold-toothed Gardner tells Stewart, "When I take this bull**** up back to Oa, they’re gonna send an army to put you down." This sounds like the perfect setup for an eventful "Lanterns" season 2 where the Lantern Corps come to take Jordan in, dead or alive. It’ll be interesting to see which of the infamous space cops they eventually send. This ain't over!

]]> <![CDATA[ The Orionid meteor shower peaks next week! Here's what to expect ]]> The Orionid meteor shower peaks overnight on Oct. 21-22, triggering a spectacular display of shooting stars as Earth plunges through the densest part of the debris trail shed by Halley's Comet. Here's what you need to know.

When is the best time to see Orionid shooting stars?

Orionid meteors are best spotted between the hours of midnight and dawn on Oct. 22, when 10-20 shooting stars may be seen brightening the night sky each hour under ideal dark-sky.

The glare cast by the 74%-lit waxing gibbous moon will hide fainter shooting stars for much of the night. Thankfully, the lunar disk will set a few hours after midnight, leaving a window of beautifully dark sky before dawn in which to enjoy the full majesty of the annual meteor shower. Remember to use a trusted website like Time and Date to discover the exact moment of moonset for your location.

Where should I look to see Orionid meteors?

Orionid shooting stars will appear to originate from a patch of sky, or radiant, located close to the red giant star Betelgeuse in the constellation Orion, which glistens above the southeastern horizon for stargazers in the U.S. during the early hours of Oct. 22.

For the best views look 40-90 degrees away from the radiant, where the glowing trains left in the wake of the fast-moving meteors will be at their longest. Be sure to head away from artificial lights and allow 20-30 minutes for your eyes to fully adapt to the dark for the best

What causes the Orionid meteor shower?

The Orionid meteor shower is active each year as Earth passes through the stream of debris left behind by Comet 1P/Halley, which was observed by a fleet of spacecraft when it last visited the inner solar system in 1986.

Shooting stars become visible when particles of the ancient comet collide with our planet's atmosphere at 147,600 miles per hour (237,539 kilometers per hour), vaporizing in a spectacular display of natural fireworks.

]]> <![CDATA[ 'It really does change you': SpaceX Crew-12 commander wishes we could all see our fragile Earth from space ]]> The astronauts of SpaceX's Crew-12 mission to the International Space Station wish that we could all see Earth as they just did.

An orbital view reveals the immense beauty of our blue planet, the only world we know of that hosts life. But it also highlights how fragile that life is, tethered to our lonely Earth in the vast void of space, according to Crew-12 commander Jessica Meir of NASA.

"You see this very thin, tenuous band of an atmosphere, and you know that that is all that is supporting life, and we really need to do our best to protect it," Meir said on Thursday afternoon (Oct. 15), during a press conference that discussed the recently concluded Crew-12 mission.

"I wish that I could bring all the eyes of all the humans to look back at the Earth in this extraordinary way that we are so privileged to have," she added. "I think it really does change you philosophically and [in] how you see each other, how you see yourself, how you see the human race when you look on it down from the vantage point that we have from above — you know, [it] gives everybody this understanding that we need to protect our planet, that it's not only so beautiful, but it's so precious."

From the International Space Station (ISS), Meir said, it's clear that everything on Earth is connected — and that the borders we've laid down between states and nations are artificial constructs.

"You realize that we really are one human when you are in space," she said. "I wish I could share that perspective with all the eyes of all the humans. I think it would be a very healthy thing for everyone to understand.

Crew-12 mission specialist Andrey Fedyaev, of the Russian space agency Roscosmos, voiced similar sentiments, though he would turn an ISS visitor's eyes inward, to focus on the crew.

"I always say that the life of crewmembers on board the space station is the best example of how people need to live on Earth," Fedyaev said during Thursday's briefing (in Russian; in interpreter translated his words into English in real time)."

"We don't have borders. We are all friendly. We're just one crew, and the safety of the crew, the safety of the station, depends on the actions of the entire crew," he added. "So, if humankind does arrive at the same conclusion — that our Earth, our planet, is one and the same space vessel that flies through space — we need to take care of it and not to destroy it. So, that's what I would like to show to everyone on Earth."

Meir and Fedyaev are far from the only ones to have their perpsectives shifted by a space mission. Pretty much every astronaut experiences this phenomenon, which is known as the overview effect, a term coined in 1987 by space philosopher Frank White.

Crew-12 consisted of Meir, Fedyaev, NASA astronaut Jack Hathaway (the mission's pilot) and the European Space Agency's Sophie Adenot (mission specialist). It was the second spaceflight for Meir and Fedyaev and the first for Hathaway and Adenot.

The quartet launched toward the ISS on Feb. 13 atop a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. Their Crew Dragon capsule, named Freedom, arrived at the orbiting lab a day later.

Crew-12 spent nearly eight months aboard the ISS, finally returning to Earth on Oct. 8. They conducted a wide range of scientific experiments and maintenance work during that time and set a few records as well.

For example, Adenot became the first French woman ever to perform a spacewalk, and she broke the mark for longest continuous spaceflight by a European at 237 days. The previous record, 201 days, was set by Luca Parmitano in 2019-2020.

]]> <![CDATA[ When not to watch a meteor shower — why I'm not staying up for the Orionids ]]> I used to think being interested in the night sky meant I had to try every meteor shower. If a calendar said "peak," I interpreted that as an instruction. I'd set an alarm, find several layers of clothing and go outside at around 2:00 a.m. when even the neighborhood cats seemed surprised to see me. Then I'd spend an increasingly resentful 45 minutes staring upward, occasionally see one meteor and wonder whether I was somehow doing it all wrong. As I've grown into stargazing, I've become much more selective.

The Orionids peak next week, and normally I'd be tempted. These fast meteors come from debris from Halley's Comet, which is enough of a connection to make almost anyone want to go outside. However, another object is in the sky this year — a big, bright waxing gibbous moon that will brighten the night sky and make "shooting stars" very hard to see.

That doesn't make the Orionids unobservable. In fact, there is a narrow window when the night sky will be free from moonlight. But it does make me far less inclined to sacrifice an entire night for them, and I certainly won't be trying to spend the night camping under a dark sky in a remote rural location far from light pollution. I've discovered that knowing when not to observe is an underrated stargazing skill.

What's happening and when to look

The Orionids are active from Oct. 2 through Nov. 7, with their 2026 maximum expected overnight on Oct. 21-22. They appear to radiate from a point near Orion, although the meteors themselves can streak across almost any part of the sky.

The shower happens because Earth crosses a stream of debris left behind by Halley's Comet, which was last in the inner solar system in 1986 and will return in 2061. Those tiny particles hit our atmosphere at roughly 41 miles (66 kilometers) per second, making Orionids particularly fast meteors.

Under ideal conditions, the International Meteor Organization gives the shower a zenithal hourly rate of 20 or more around maximum. But "zenithal hourly rate" is not the same as promising that I will personally see 20 meteors while standing in my backyard for an hour. It assumes an excellent dark sky, a well-placed radiant and unobstructed viewing. In reality, that's impossible — at the very least you'd have to have eyes in the back of your head. And on each side.

This year adds another complication. The moon reaches first quarter on Oct. 18 and continues waxing toward full on Oct. 26. On the peak night of the Orionids, an 80%-illuminated waxing gibbous moon will be in the night sky as it gets dark on Oct. 21 and sets around 03:00 a.m. local time across Europe and North America on Oct. 22. You can probably see the workaround. Sunrise is roughly 06:30 a.m. local time, which means astronomical darkness — when the sun is more than 18 degrees below the horizon, meaning complete darkness — lasts until around 05:00 a.m. local time (these times work as a ballpark, but you can (check the exact times of moonset and sunrise for your location on Time and Date).

So there is a dark window before dawn, and that is when I would try to see the shower if I were determined to see it. The Orionid radiant is also much better placed after midnight than it is in the evening.

Knowing exactly what's going to happen in the sky turns a casual meteor watch into a rather more calculated exercise.

How and when I'm watching it

My plan for the Orionids this year is the same as usual — after checking the moon phase and the moonset and sunrise times, there's one more variable. The weather forecast first.

If the forecast is excellent and I'm feeling enthusiastic, I'll target the period after moonset and before morning twilight on Oct. 22. If it's due to be cloudy, I'm staying in bed.

This sounds obvious, but I think beginners are sometimes given the impression that successful stargazing requires heroic commitment. It doesn't. A meteor shower is not a performance that disappears the moment the advertised "peak" passes. The Orionids have a relatively broad period of activity, so meteors can appear on nights either side of maximum, too.

If I do go outside at 3:00 a.m., I'll do so without two hugely valuable resources for meteor showers — a lawn chair and bags of patience.

Stargazer's corner: October 16-22, 2026

The moon reaches first quarter on Oct. 18, making stargazing tricky this week. That means I'm changing what I observe rather than declaring the week a write-off. The moon itself becomes an excellent target in early evening around first quarter. Sunlight strikes the lunar landscape along the terminator — the boundary between lunar day and night — throwing mountains and crater rims into strong relief. A cheap pair of binoculars can reveal a surprising amount. With a telescope, you can spend hours getting lost in the Montes Apenninus mountain range and three nearby craters — Eratosthenes and Archimedes on either side, and Plato above. Saturn remains another easy evening target after its Oct. 4 opposition. Look toward the eastern and southeastern sky after dark for its steady yellowish light. Even a modest telescope pointed at Saturn's rings will astound.

Constellation of the week: Cassiopeia

Cassiopeia is one of the easiest constellations I know to find because its five main stars form a conspicuous W — or, right now, something that looks suspiciously more like an M. Look toward the northern sky in the evening. From mid-northern latitudes, Cassiopeia is high and prominent during autumn, on the opposite side of Polaris from the Big Dipper. That relationship is more useful to me than memorizing exactly which way the W should point. Cassiopeia circles Polaris as Earth rotates, so its orientation changes through the night. From sufficiently northerly locations, it's circumpolar, meaning it never sets below the horizon.

Cassiopeia is one of the easiest constellations I know to find because its five main stars form a conspicuous W — or, right now, something that looks suspiciously more like an M. Look toward the northern sky in the evening. From mid-northern latitudes, Cassiopeia is high and prominent during autumn, on the opposite side of Polaris from the Big Dipper. That relationship is more useful to me than memorizing exactly which way the W should point. Cassiopeia circles Polaris as Earth rotates, so its orientation changes through the night. From sufficiently northerly locations, it's circumpolar, meaning it never sets below the horizon.

]]>

 <description>Česko bude mít 27 nových senátorů. Pět z nich zvolili lidé už před týdnem v prvním kole, o dalších 22 rozhodli v pátek a v sobotu.    <title>Štěnice zrušily let z Itálie. Přímo v letadle lezly po oblečení i zavazadlech</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/svet/stenice-v-letadle-z-italie-do-australie/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=svet</link>
   <description>Cestující aerolinky Qantas poštípaly počátkem října během letu z australského Perthu do italského Říma štěnice. Hmyz jim lezl po oblečení, zavazadlech i dekách. Postižení dostali antihistaminika na zmírnění svědění, zásoby léků však palubnímu personálu nakonec došly. Kvůli důkladnému vyčištění letadla aerolinka následně zrušila navazující zpáteční spoj.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Průšvih a zrada. Skončí Chorý ve Slavii? Jeho prostředníček řeší i ve Francii</title>
   <link>https://www.denik.cz/ostatni-fotbal/tomas-chory-prostrednicek-vylouceni-cervena-karta-zkrat-slavia-hradec-reakce/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=ostatni-fotbal</link>
   <description>Další průšvih, další bouřlivá debata. Kanonýr a reprezentant Tomáš Chorý předvedl další exces. Slávistický útočník ukázal v ligovém utkání proti Hradci Králové (0:0) vulgární gesto. Za zdvižený prostředníček směrem k rozhodčímu Janu Všetečkovi dostal červenou kartu. Pro problematického fotbalistu tím skončil nejen zápas, ale možná i angažmá v Edenu.</description>

  <item>
   <title>Měl svou paničku jen pro sebe. Teď Tobík v Jestřebí čeká na nový domov</title>
   <link>https://ceskolipsky.denik.cz/zpravy-region/mel-svou-panicku-jen-pro-sebe-ted-tobik-v-jestrebi-ceka-na-novy-domov/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed-vse&utm_campaign=ceskolipsky.denik.cz&utm_content=zpravy-region</link>
   <description>Jedenáctiletý Tobík toho od nového života nechce mnoho. Klidný domov, vlastní pelíšek, procházky a především člověka, kterému bude moci znovu dělat věrného parťáka. Kříženec, který byl zvyklý žít se svou paničkou, nyní čeká na druhou šanci v útulku Dogsy v Jestřebí na Českolipsku.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Samotáři, Šeptej a Kluci to vidí jinak než holky. Nejen Ondříček točil generační filmy</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/kultura/film-televize/deti-noci-kluci-to-vidi-jinak-nez-holky-ondricek.A261015_110956_filmvideo_spm#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Sedm pražských mostů, sedm propojených osudů. Autorský snímek Davida Ondříčka Kluci to vidí jinak než holky navazuje volně svou náladou na režisérovu prvotinu Šeptej, která se stala generačním kultem i dokumentem 90. let se zrozením tuzemské klubové scény. Dnes tady zní jiná hudba, ale lidé, kteří ve světlech nočního velkoměsta hledají únik ze samoty, se ve své podstatě příliš nemění.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Ostrava je rozhodnutá. Třetí největší město povedou ANO a Starostové s Ostravakem</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/volby/ostrava/koalice-ostrava-ano-veres-starostove-bohac-ostravak-motoriste.A261018_100458_ostrava-volby_jog#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Povolební vyjednávání v Ostravě skončilo. Vítězné hnutí ANO a už dříve dohodnutý partner Starostové pro Ostravu přibrali do trojkoalice místní hnutí Ostravak. V opozici tak zůstali zastupitelé Motoristů a sdružení srdcOVA, tedy ODS, KDU-ČSL a TOP 09. Primátorem bude 31letý Richard Vereš (ANO).</description>

    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Nová jízdní kola nesou logo shořelé 34. budovy. Je to nostalgie, říká výrobce</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zlin/zpravy/zlin-budova-34-pozar-equator-cycling.A261016_112921_zlin-zpravy_epfoj#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Zlínská rodinná firma Equator Cycling byla jedna z těch, které působily ve 34. budově zlínského baťovského areálu. V létě jí tam při jejím požáru shořelo úplně vše: sklady, kanceláře, dílna. Její většinový majitel Milan Šimek vážně zvažoval, jestli bude začínat znovu. Ale obrovská morální i finanční podpora lidí ho k tomu prakticky přinutily.</description>

    <item>
      <title>Rusko podniklo 76 útoků od oznámení Trumpova příměří, napsal Zelenskyj</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/ukrajina-rusko-valka-zelenskyj-trump-zaporozi.A261018_125636_zahranicni_jhr#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Rusko vyslalo v noci na neděli na Ukrajinu 180 dronů a balistickou střelu, přičemž protivzdušná obrana zneškodnila 152 bezpilotních letounů, oznámilo ráno ukrajinské letectvo. Prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj uvedl, že údery zabily dva lidi, dalších 12 včetně dětí utrpěli zranění. Podle něj Rusko podniká desítky útoky od začátku energetického příměří oznámeného americkým prezidentem Donaldem Trumpem. </description>

      <description>Litvav neděli ráno vyhlásila ve středních a severních regionech země červený stupeň leteckého poplachu a jejich obyvatele vyzvala, aby se odebrali do úkrytů.     <item>
      <title>Žádné vyjednávaní. Putinova bezpečnostní zóna ukazuje na maximalistické cíle</title>
      <link>https://www.idnes.cz/zpravy/zahranicni/ukrajina-putin-rusko-ukrajina-charkovska-sumska-oblast-doneck-valka.A261017_120552_zahranicni_jhr#utm_source=rss&utm_medium=feed&utm_campaign=zpravodaj&utm_content=main</link>
      <description>Ruský prezident Vladimir Putin prohlásil, že Rusko vytváří uvnitř Ukrajiny podél společných hranic „bezpečnostní zónu“. O ní nehodlá s Kyjevem při jakýchkoli budoucích diskuzích vůbec vyjednávat. Tato zóna má obsahovat i části Sumské a Charkovské oblasti, na které si Rusko v mírových jednáních neklade nárok. Ukazuje to tudíž maximalistické ambice Putina.</description>

<title>Jednotné měsíční hlášení zaměstnavatele se stát chystá rozšířit o další údaje, navrhuje i dosud nefungující sdílení</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/jednotne-mesicni-hlaseni-zamestnavatele-se-stat-chysta-rozsirit-o-dalsi-udaje-navrhuje-i-dosud-nefungujici-sdileni/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Jednotné měsíční hlá&#353;ení zaměstnavatele (JMHZ) má státu umožnit sbírat dal&#353;í údaje o zaměstnancích a zpřístupnit je více úřadům. Ministerstvo práce a sociálních věcí navrhuje změny, které mají reagovat na novou legislativu i praktické potřeby státních institucí. K návrhu přibyly nové dokumenty v oficiálním systému ODok.</description>

<title>Americký Groupon bude pod taktovkou Čechů prodávat přes AI agenty</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/americky-groupon-bude-pod-taktovkou-cechu-prodavat-pres-ai-agenty/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Někdej&#353;í internetový fenomén hromadných slev Groupon, který kormidlují Če&#353;i z Pale Fire Capial, se otevřel obchodování, při kterém si zážitky nemají kupovat lidé, ale dělat to za ně mají AI agenti. Nově spu&#353;těná platforma LivingSocial jim umožňuje vyhledávat a porovnávat zážitky a připravit nákup. Nabízí přes 50 tisíc aktivit napříč Spojenými státy.</description>

<item>
<title>Česko pomáhá rozhýbat evropský čipový průmysl. Nová služba vývojářům ušetří hromadu práce</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/cesko-pomaha-rozhybat-evropsky-cipovy-prumysl-nova-sluzba-vyvojarum-usetri-hromadu-prace/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Český národní polovodičový klastr ve spolupráci s Českým polovodičovým centrem vytvořily užitečný online nástroj. Jde o katalog takzvaných IP bloků používaných při vývoji čipů. Tyto bloky v katalogu nabízí firmy a organizace z Evropy. Cílem je polovodičovým návrhářům nabídnout jednoduchý přístup ke klíčovým technologiím, které jsou ověřené a rychle nasaditelné a není je nutné vynalézat znovu.</description>

<item>
<title>Miliarda jim trvala tři roky, druhá jen pět měsíců. Českou AI naději už používají Meta, Xiaomi nebo Nvidia</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/miliarda-jim-trvala-tri-roky-druha-jen-pet-mesicu-ceskou-ai-nadeji-uz-pouzivaji-meta-xiaomi-nebo-nvidia/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Český startup E2B aktuálně patří k největ&#353;ím technologickým nadějím země. Pro AI agenty umožňuje velice rychle spou&#353;tět sandboxy, tedy izolovaná prostředí, v nichž agenti mohou běžet, vykonat práci a sandbox následně ukončit. E2B pokračuje v silném růstu. Firma informovala, že jí trvalo tři roky, než u ní zákazníci rozjeli miliardu sandboxů. Teď pokočila metu dvou miliard sandboxů s tím, že druhá miliarda trvala pouze pět měsíců.</description>

 <description>Tibet je od 50. let okupován Čínou. „V historii národa není 80 let moc dlouhá doba. Jako buddhisté věříme v pomíjivost. Uvidíme, jak dlouho dokáže komunismus přežít,“ říká pro Vertikálu Českého rozhlasu Plus prezident Ústřední tibetské správy v exilu Penpa Cchering, který navštívil pražské Forum 2000.  <description>Spojené státy chtějí, aby Izrael podnikl důraznější kroky k zamezení útokům, kterých se na Západním břehu Jordánu dopouští židovští osadníci. V sobotu to podle agentury Reuters uvedl americký ministr zahraničí Marco Rubio.</description>

 <description>Ruská protivzdušná obrana v noci na neděli zneškodnila 1015 ukrajinských dronů nad 15 ruskými regiony, poloostrovem Krym a Černým mořem, uvedlo ráno ministerstvo obrany v Moskvě. Terčem úderu se stal v noci Petrohrad, sdělil na platformě Telegram gubernátor města Alexandr Beglov.  Podle údajů ruské armády jde o jeden z nejrozsáhlejších nočních útoků od zahájení ruské války proti Ukrajině, podotkla BBC.</description>

 <description>Francouzský prezident Macron večer projedná s premiérem a členy vlády násilnosti ze soboty a ve 20.00 promluví k národu, informují francouzská média. V souvislosti se sobotními demonstracemi, násilím a rabováním, které je provázely, bylo v Paříži zadrženo rekordních 855 lidí.  <description>Litva v neděli ráno vyhlásila ve středních a severních regionech země červený stupeň leteckého poplachu a jejich obyvatele vyzvala, aby se odebrali do úkrytů.  <description>Dne 15. listopadu 2020 odešla běloruská televizní reportérka Kaciaryna Andrejevová Bakhvalavová do práce, domů už se ale nikdy nevrátila. Díky americké diplomacii ji však po pěti letech propustili a z Běloruska deportovali. „Až to bude bezpečné, určitě se do země vrátím. Mám ji ráda,“ říká pro Český rozhlas Plus novinářka.</description>

 <description>Už pátý měsíc Albánci protestují proti vládě Ediho Ramy ve hnutí, které odstartoval na konci května začátek prací v chráněné přírodní oblasti Vjosa-Narta, kde chce zeť Donalda Trumpa Jared Kushner postavit luxusní resort.  <description>Židovští osadníci v sobotu na okupovaném Západním břehu Jordánu napadli delegaci, ve které byli diplomaté z několika zemí EU. Napsala to izraelská média i palestinská agentura WAFA. Osadníci útočí na Palestince a mezinárodní aktivisty při sklizni oliv. Událost začala vyšetřovat izraelská policie. Útok odsoudili izraelský ministr zahraničí Gideon Saar, šéf belgické diplomacie Maxime Prevot i polské ministerstvo zahraničí. </description>

<item>
 <title>Rušení sankcí proti Rusku bude pokračovat, nafta byla jen prvním krokem, míní Zelenskyj</title>
 <link>https://www.irozhlas.cz/zpravy-svet/online-ruseni-sankci-proti-rusku-bude-pokracovat-nafta-byla-jen-prvnim-krokem_2610171541_brz</link>
 <description>Spojené státy budou pokračovat v rušení sankcí proti Rusku, dohoda o naftě byla pouze prvním krokem. Takové očekávání dal v sobotu v komunikaci s novináři najevo ukrajinský prezident Volodymyr Zelenskyj. Prezident Donald Trump před několika dny oznámil, že se s ruským protějškem Vladimirem Putinem dohodl na dodávkách nafty na americký a světový trh. V pátek šéf Bílého domu podepsal příkaz, který pozastavuje sankce mířené proti ruské ekonomice.</description>

<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/jednotne-mesicni-hlaseni-zamestnavatele-se-stat-chysta-rozsirit-o-dalsi-udaje-navrhuje-i-dosud-nefungujici-sdileni/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Jednotné měsíční hlá&#353;ení zaměstnavatele (JMHZ) má státu umožnit sbírat dal&#353;í údaje o zaměstnancích a zpřístupnit je více úřadům. Ministerstvo práce a sociálních věcí navrhuje změny, které mají reagovat na novou legislativu i praktické potřeby státních institucí. K návrhu přibyly nové dokumenty v oficiálním systému ODok.</description>

<description>Někdej&#353;í internetový fenomén hromadných slev Groupon, který kormidlují Če&#353;i z Pale Fire Capial, se otevřel obchodování, při kterém si zážitky nemají kupovat lidé, ale dělat to za ně mají AI agenti. Nově spu&#353;těná platforma LivingSocial jim umožňuje vyhledávat a porovnávat zážitky a připravit nákup. Nabízí přes 50 tisíc aktivit napříč Spojenými státy.</description>

<item>
<title>Česko pomáhá rozhýbat evropský čipový průmysl. Nová služba vývojářům ušetří hromadu práce</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/cesko-pomaha-rozhybat-evropsky-cipovy-prumysl-nova-sluzba-vyvojarum-usetri-hromadu-prace/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Český národní polovodičový klastr ve spolupráci s Českým polovodičovým centrem vytvořily užitečný online nástroj. Jde o katalog takzvaných IP bloků používaných při vývoji čipů. Tyto bloky v katalogu nabízí firmy a organizace z Evropy. Cílem je polovodičovým návrhářům nabídnout jednoduchý přístup ke klíčovým technologiím, které jsou ověřené a rychle nasaditelné a není je nutné vynalézat znovu.</description>

<item>
<title>Miliarda jim trvala tři roky, druhá jen pět měsíců. Českou AI naději už používají Meta, Xiaomi nebo Nvidia</title>
<link>https://www.lupa.cz/aktuality/miliarda-jim-trvala-tri-roky-druha-jen-pet-mesicu-ceskou-ai-nadeji-uz-pouzivaji-meta-xiaomi-nebo-nvidia/?utm_source=rss&utm_medium=text&utm_campaign=rss</link>
<description>Český startup E2B aktuálně patří k největ&#353;ím technologickým nadějím země. Pro AI agenty umožňuje velice rychle spou&#353;tět sandboxy, tedy izolovaná prostředí, v nichž agenti mohou běžet, vykonat práci a sandbox následně ukončit. E2B pokračuje v silném růstu. Firma informovala, že jí trvalo tři roky, než u ní zákazníci rozjeli miliardu sandboxů. Teď pokočila metu dvou miliard sandboxů s tím, že druhá miliarda trvala pouze pět měsíců.</description>

news.rawText:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<rss version="2.0" xmlns:dc="http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/"><channel><title>Liberecká Drbna</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz</link><description>Liberecká Drbna</description><language>cs</language><item><title>Finanční gramotnost dětí klesá, testy ve školách čím dál častěji řeší umělá inteligence</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903157-financni-gramotnost-deti-klesa-testy-ve-skolach-cim-dal-casteji-resi-umela-inteligence.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903157-financni-gramotnost-deti-klesa-testy-ve-skolach-cim-dal-casteji-resi-umela-inteligence.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 11:58:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Kateřina Pospěchová</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Úroveň finanční gramotnosti u dětí v Česku klesá a tradiční formy testování narážejí na technologické limity. Žáci si při testech stále častěji pomáhají generativní umělou inteligencí. Ukazuje to nejnovější zpráva České školní inspekce a zkušenosti z minulého ročníku Soutěže Finanční gramotnost.</description></item><item><title>KSČM už není skutečná levice. Klesla do pozice jakéhosi béčka SPD, říká Jiří Dolejš</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903181-kscm-uz-neni-skutecna-levice-klesla-do-pozice-jakehosi-becka-spd-rika-jiri-dolejs.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903181-kscm-uz-neni-skutecna-levice-klesla-do-pozice-jakehosi-becka-spd-rika-jiri-dolejs.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:34:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Michael Daněk</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Bývalý poslanec a dlouholetý člen KSČM Jiří Dolejš kritizuje směřování své někdejší strany. Podle něj opustila snahu o modernizaci, přiblížila se krajní pravici a ztratila důvěru voličů. V rozhovoru pro Drbnu mluví také o budoucnosti levice a o tom, proč její obnova musí začít prakticky od začátku.</description></item><item><title>Stovky onemocnění od klíšťat v Libereckém kraji. Riziko trvá i na podzim</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903191-stovky-onemocneni-od-klistat-v-libereckem-kraji-riziko-trva-i-na-podzim.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/spolecnost/903191-stovky-onemocneni-od-klistat-v-libereckem-kraji-riziko-trva-i-na-podzim.html</guid><pubDate>Sun, 18 Oct 2026 07:01:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Společnost</category><description>Za prvních devět měsíců roku bylo v Libereckém kraji hlášeno 31 případů klíšťové encefalitidy a 728 případů lymeské borreliózy. Celkem jde o 759 případů obou infekcí. Podle odborníků ale riziko nakažení trvá i během podzimu.</description></item><item><title>Slovan prohrál v Olomouci 0:1, dva góly mu odvolal VAR</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903315-slovan-prohral-v-olomouci-0-1-dva-goly-mu-odvolal-var.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/fotbal/903315-slovan-prohral-v-olomouci-0-1-dva-goly-mu-odvolal-var.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 20:23:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Fotbal</category><description>Liberečtí fotbalisté v lize podruhé za sebou prohráli a potřetí nedali gól. V Olomouci tedy skórovali hned třikrát, jenže ani jeden z gólů neplatil. A protože branka domácích z 11. minuty byla v pořádku, Slovan prohrál 0:1.</description></item><item><title>Nový senátor Půta se vzdá imunity ve své korupční kauze</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903310-novy-senator-puta-se-vzda-imunity-ve-sve-korupcni-kauze.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903310-novy-senator-puta-se-vzda-imunity-ve-sve-korupcni-kauze.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 17:47:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>ČTK</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Liberecký hejtman Martin Půta (Starostové pro Liberecký kraj), který byl zvolen do Senátu za obvod Česká Lípa, senátorské imunity nevyužije. Půta je nepravomocně odsouzen v korupční kauze, v níž ale vinu odmítá.</description></item><item><title>Hejtman Půta míří do Senátu, ve druhém kole porazil Jitku Volfovou</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903290-hejtman-puta-miri-do-senatu-ve-druhem-kole-porazil-jitku-volfovou.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/politika/903290-hejtman-puta-miri-do-senatu-ve-druhem-kole-porazil-jitku-volfovou.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 15:10:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Politika</category><description>Senátorem za Českolipsko a část Liberecka a Mělnicka bude v následujícím volebním období dlouholetý hejtman Libereckého kraje Martin Půta (Starostové pro LK). Ten ve druhém kole porazil končící starostku České Lípy Jitku Volfovou (ANO). Ta tak zůstává poslankyní.</description></item><item><title>Místo psychologa chatbot. S AI řeší trápení už třetina dospělých</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903156-misto-psychologa-chatbot-s-ai-resi-trapeni-uz-tretina-dospelych.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/zdravi/903156-misto-psychologa-chatbot-s-ai-resi-trapeni-uz-tretina-dospelych.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 13:25:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Hanka Poskočilová</dc:creator><category>Zdraví</category><description>Máte trápení? Možná ho dneska dřív než kamarádovi svěříte umělé inteligenci. Podle nového průzkumu už to dělá třetina dospělých a mezi mladými dokonce více než polovina.</description></item><item><title>Kamion v noci zablokoval silnici z Turnova na Malou Skálu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903275-kamion-v-noci-zablokoval-silnici-z-turnova-na-malou-skalu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903275-kamion-v-noci-zablokoval-silnici-z-turnova-na-malou-skalu.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 11:38:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>K dopravní nehodě došlo v noci na sobotu na silnici číslo 10 mezi Turnovem a Malou Skálou. Kamion silnici v Borku zcela zablokoval.</description></item><item><title>Pozor na linky 21 a 56 MHD v Liberci: Zastávka Školní je jinde. Kdy se vrátí zpět?</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903238-pozor-na-linky-21-a-56-mhd-v-liberci-zastavka-skolni-je-jinde-kdy-se-vrati-zpet.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/doprava/903238-pozor-na-linky-21-a-56-mhd-v-liberci-zastavka-skolni-je-jinde-kdy-se-vrati-zpet.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 11:00:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Martina Petrášková</dc:creator><category>Doprava</category><description>Cestující městskou hromadnou dopravou v Liberci musejí počítat se změnou u linek na Králově háji. Kvůli stavebním pracím došlo v tomto týdnu k přesunu zastávky Školní pro autobusové linky 21 a 56 ve směru do centra. Kde teď zastávku cestující najdou a kdy se vrátí na své původní místo?</description></item><item><title>Zuzana Kocumová vyhrála světový titul ve Spartan sprintu</title><link>https://liberecka.drbna.cz/ostatni-sporty/903188-zuzana-kocumova-vyhrala-svetovy-titul-ve-spartan-sprintu.html</link><guid isPermaLink="true">https://liberecka.drbna.cz/ostatni-sporty/903188-zuzana-kocumova-vyhrala-svetovy-titul-ve-spartan-sprintu.html</guid><pubDate>Sat, 17 Oct 2026 09:23:00 +0200</pubDate><dc:creator>Luboš Vrabec</dc:creator><category>Ostatní sporty</category><description>Liberecká závodnice a politička Zuzana Kocumová dosáhla v posledních týdnech dvou velkých sportovních úspěchů. Po titulu mistryně Evropy v závodech Spartan ovládla také sprint na světovém šampionátu v chorvatském Hvaru.</description></item></channel></rss>

výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu dobrý den ze šluknovského výběžku, konce světa - šluknovský výběžek Sat, 17 Oct 2026 16:29:52 +0000 cs hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.3 https://www.vybezek.eu/wp-uploads/2018/09/cropped-favicon-vybezek-32x32.png výběžek.eu https://www.vybezek.eu 32 32 Víkend Křišťálového údolí 2 – Den otevřených dveří Sklářského muzea (Kamenický Šenov 2026) https://www.vybezek.eu/295953-vikend-kristaloveho-udoli-2-den-otevrenych-dveri-sklarskeho-muzea-kamenicky-senov-2026/ Sat, 17 Oct 2026 16:29:52 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=295953 Víkend 17. a 18. října 2026 v Libereckém kraji opět ve znamení Křišťálového údolí, znovu se otevřely brány a dveře v mnoha sklárnách, ateliérech, výrobních provozech, muzeích a školách.

Těch míst je plno křížem krážem přes celý kraj. Už dlouho se opakovaně kochávám v Preciose, byl jsem kdysi také v Novém Boru v Crystalexu, a letos jsem si řekl, že nikam nespěchám a když už jsem jednou v Kamenickém Šenově, okouknu zas jednou místní muzeum. Rekonstrukce stále probíhá, takže funguje v minimalistickém režimu. Nicméně poseděl jsem, pokoukal a hlavně pokecal. A i o tom tenhle křišťálový víkend přece má být…

2025 ->, 2023 ->, 2019 ->, 2017 ->

Víkend 17. a 18. října 2026 v Libereckém kraji opět ve znamení Křišťálového údolí, znovu se otevřely brány a dveře v mnoha sklárnách, ateliérech, výrobních provozech, muzeích a školách.

Je jedno, kolikrát už, prostě jsem opět vyrazil do Kamenického Šenova, protože tam to pokaždé stojí za podívání. A letos jsem se rozhodl nezůstat jen tam.

Trasa opět obměněná a ve dvou variantách, týmy organizátorů s úsměvem od parkoviště do nejzazších koutů areálu.

Prodej, soutěže, dílničky. Asi jediná velká změna, které jsem si všiml – letos si návštěvníci neměli možnost sami fouknout na huti. I tak musím znovu konstatovat – kdykoli zas!

2025 ->, 2023 ->, 2019 ->, 2017 ->

]]> Podzimní hry 2026 – malá kopaná https://www.vybezek.eu/295858-podzimni-hry-2026-mala-kopana/ Fri, 16 Oct 2026 10:23:12 +0000 https://www.vybezek.eu/?p=295858 Ve středu 14. října 2026 se na umělém trávníku v areálu Kotliny ve Varnsdorfu uskutečnil druhý díl letošních podzimních her, tentokrát v malé kopané.

Turnaje se zúčastnila čtyři chlapecká družstva, která mezi sebou poměřila své síly systémem každý s každým. Jednotlivá utkání se hrála na 15 minut.

Naši chlapci vstupovali do turnaje s jasným cílem, kterým bylo obhájit prvenství z loňského roku. Hned v úvodním utkání proti ZŠ Východní předvedli výborný výkon a zaslouženě zvítězili vysoko 8:0. Ve druhém zápase je čekalo družstvo Gymnázia Varnsdorf. Díky skvělému vstupu do utkání a zodpovědnému výkonu si naši hráči připsali další přesvědčivé vítězství, tentokrát 4:0. V posledním utkání se naši chlapci utkali s družstvem ZŠ Edisonova. Přestože si během zápasu vytvořili řadu slibných brankových příležitostí, jejich neproměňování přineslo dramatickou koncovku. Nakonec však dokázali těsné vedení udržet a po vítězství 3:2 mohli slavit zasloužený triumf.

Naši fotbalisté tak prošli celým turnajem bez ztráty jediného bodu, s celkovým skóre 15:2, a úspěšně obhájili loňské prvenství!
